These sliders only change the lyrics shown on your car or Bluetooth screen. Your phone\'s synced lyrics stay exactly the same.
No Bluetooth device connected — editing the default timing offset

Car screens fit only a little text at a time, so each lyric line is cut into small pieces that show one after another. The sliders below decide how big each piece is and how quickly they change. Fast, wordy songs like small pieces that flip quickly; slower songs can hold bigger pieces for longer. Pick a preset to start, then fine-tune.

Fixes lyrics that reach the car too early or too late. Slide right if lines show up behind the music, so each one is sent a little earlier. Slide left if they jump ahead of the song. Your phone lyrics are not touched.

How much of a line to show at once. Keep it small so each piece is short and easy to read at a glance on a small screen. Make it larger to fit more words per piece, so long lines get split apart less often.

How much long text you let scroll past instead of splitting it up. Raise it if your car scrolls smoothly and you can keep up with fast-moving text, so long lines stay in one piece. Lower it toward zero if text slides away before you finish reading, so long lines are chopped into smaller pieces.

The shortest time each piece stays before the next one replaces it. Raise it to hold every piece longer so you get more time to read, even if the lyrics fall a little behind fast lines. Lower it to let pieces flip by quickly and keep pace with rapid songs.
